attempts.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9, cronie), created the opsadmin user and wrote /etc/cron.allow containing exactly `root` and `opsadmin`, removing any /etc/cron.deny so the allow-list is authoritative. Verified root and opsadmin can install crontabs via `crontab`, and that an arbitrary non-listed user is rejected with "not allowed to use this program (crontab)". Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and cron.allow state, issued a non-interactive `reboot` whose ack returned before disconnection, polled until the node came back, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified crond is active, /etc/cron.allow is unchanged, root/opsadmin can still schedule cron jobs, and a newly-created non-allowed test user is still denied post-restart.
